Design kit

Showcase

Every foundation and component of the kit, live, in one scroll. Switch the theme to check light, dark and high contrast; each section shows the markup to copy. Generated by npm run build from tokens/tokens.json and showcase/*.html.

Theme
Contrast

Colour --gw-color-*

Semantic tokens only: components never reference a hex value. Each swatch follows the current theme; values read light · dark. Every text and non-text pair is verified for WCAG 2.2 AA in light, dark and both high contrast modes by npm run check (tokens/contrast-pairs.json).

Typography gw-type()

Inter for the interface: drawn for screens, tabular figures, full Cyrillic, and the cv05 / cv08 alternates on so l, I and 1 never read alike. JetBrains Mono for everything literal: tool names, slugs, hosts, SQL, tokens, JSON. Ligatures are off in mono, because what a human approves must be exactly what runs. Both are self-hosted (OFL 1.1).

Icons and logo gw-icon gw-icon-tile gw-logo

Lucide only, pinned and shipped in vendor/lucide (the app uses lucide-angular at the same version). Icons are decorative by default (aria-hidden): the text next to them carries the meaning. Check a name with npm run icons -- --search shield; npm run check fails on a name that does not exist.

Buttons gw-btn

One primitive for every action. Primary marks the one main action of a view. Approve (green) exists only for the approval decision, so green always means "let it run". Danger is the confirming step of something irreversible; danger ghost is the trigger that opens that confirmation. Labels are a verb and an object, in sentence case.

Cards gw-card gw-stack

The one container. Header with a title, an optional one-line description and actions on the right; body; optional footer. Stack cards with gw-stack so the gap is always --gw-space-4.

App shell gw-shell gw-titlebar gw-sidebar gw-nav

The one window frame of the app: titlebar across the top, sidebar on the left, main on the right. The window never scrolls as a whole; the sidebar body and main scroll on their own. Every page copies the shell verbatim from pages/_shell.html and changes only the title, aria-current and the page content. Do not build a second navigation, a page-level sidebar or a custom header: sub-navigation inside a page is gw-tabs, settings groups are the settings-layout element.

Expanded and collapsed

Left: the default 240px sidebar. Right: .gw-shell[data-collapsed], set by the panel button (data-gw-sidebar-toggle; kit.js keeps aria-expanded in sync and remembers the choice across pages) and applied automatically below 960px. Collapsed, labels stay in the accessibility tree, groups are split by hairlines, the Approvals counter becomes an amber dot on the icon, and hovering or tabbing to an icon shows its label beside it. Markup: copy pages/_shell.html.

Without sidebar

Onboarding and the core status screen use the same frame without gw-sidebar: main spans the full width under the titlebar, usually with a gw-page--narrow inside. Everything app-wide that is not navigation, such as a gw-alert--banner, goes first inside gw-shell__main, never as a fourth child of the grid.

Get started

Set up GateRook

Protect the master key, add a connection, create an endpoint and connect an AI app.

Titlebar

The whole bar is an Electron drag region; links, buttons, labels and popovers inside opt out automatically. gw-titlebar--mac (second bar) reserves the traffic-light inset plus a small gap before Back; on Windows and Linux the Window Controls Overlay area is reserved through env(titlebar-area-*). The section title stays centered in the window and truncates before the controls. Back is disabled until an earlier application page exists; its enabled and disabled states are shown below. Actions: search with its shortcut, the approvals bell with an attention counter, the appearance popover (theme and contrast). The popover title is not a heading: the titlebar comes before the page h1.

Sidebar and navigation

Items are links with aria-current="page" on the current one: selected fill, primary text, semibold and a 2px brand bar, so the state never rests on colour alone. Groups follow the questions the app answers (Resources: what is connected, Access: who gets in and how, Observe: what agents did) and are role="group" labelled by their overline. Settings sits at the bottom. The footer always shows the local core and the tunnel, in words; the core dot stays still (never gw-status--live here: a dot that pulses on every screen forever fails WCAG 2.2.2).

Page header gw-page-header gw-breadcrumb

The top of every page and the home of its one h1: breadcrumb on nested pages, title with a one-sentence description, meta (status, URL, counts), actions on the right and an optional tab row. Actions wrap under the heading when the window narrows. Not for card or section titles (use gw-card__title and gw-section__title), and never twice on a page.

Page layout gw-page gw-section gw-toolbar gw-split gw-grid gw-divider

Arrangement only: these classes place cards, tables and forms inside gw-shell__main; they draw no surfaces of their own. gw-page is the only way to cap a width, so never set max-width or margin: 0 auto on page content.

Page widths

Default: up to 1440px of content with 32px gutters (16px below 640px), sections 32px apart. gw-page--narrow caps content at 880px for forms and settings read top to bottom. gw-page--full has no cap and fills main's height, so a gw-split inside it takes the remaining height (Approvals, Playground, Activity).

gw-page--narrow · Settings, Connection form, Policies
gw-page · Overview, Connections, Endpoints, AI apps
gw-page--full · Activity, Approvals, Playground

Section

A titled block of a page without a card around it: h2, an optional one-line description and actions on the right. Use a card instead when the block needs its own surface or footer.

Keys, avatars, client marks gw-kbd gw-avatar gw-client-mark

Small identity and hint marks. Keys show a shortcut in running text, help and the command palette. Avatars are people (approvers, users in server mode): circles. Client marks are MCP clients: rounded squares with a neutral monogram, never a vendor logo. Official marks come only from vendor press kits, after sign-off.

Keyboard keys

One kbd per key, written as text (Esc, Enter, Shift). Arrows and Return are Lucide icons with screen reader text. Inside a button use gw-btn__kbd instead.

Press ⌘K to search, Esc to close.

Move with Up arrowDown arrow, run with Enter.

Approve the open request with ⌘ShiftEnter.

<p class="gw-text-body-read">Move with <kbd class="gw-kbd"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="arrow-up"></i><span class="gw-sr-only">Up arrow</span></kbd><kbd class="gw-kbd"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="arrow-down"></i><span class="gw-sr-only">Down arrow</span></kbd>, run with <kbd class="gw-kbd"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="corner-down-left"></i><span class="gw-sr-only">Enter</span></kbd>.</p>

Avatars

Two initials on a neutral circle, or a photo in __img. Next to a visible name the avatar is aria-hidden; alone it is role="img" with the full name. Sizes: --sm 20 (table rows, timelines), default 28, --lg 40 (account, users). People appear only in server mode (Users and roles, a server-mode preview); the desktop app has one local user, so its history says “by you” and needs no avatar.

Badges and counters gw-badge gw-counter

A badge names a state in a word or two: the decision on a call, the lifetime of a token, the kind of a connector. The tone, icon and words come from one vocabulary (BLUEPRINT §7), so "Denied by policy" looks the same in Activity, Approvals and Insights. Badges are display only: a removable value or an active filter is a tag, an environment is the env marker, a toggle is a pressed button. A counter is a bare number next to a nav item, tab or button; amber means a human is waiting.

Decisions on a call

Allowed Approved Waiting for approval Denied by policy Rejected Expired Error

Counters

A number alone means little to a screen reader: add hidden context ("3 waiting") or make sure the control's name says what is counted. Default is a plain count, attention (amber) means a human is waiting, muted is a quiet count beside a label.

Status, environment, mode gw-status gw-env gw-mode

Three small markers that answer "is it working", "where does it run" and "what may the agent do". Status is a dot and words for the health of a connection, the core, the tunnel or an AI app; the words always say the state, the dot is the second cue. Env marks dev, stage or prod next to a connection name in every risky context; its shape (straight bar, mono capitals) keeps it apart from a status pill. Mode shows a tool's mode where it cannot be changed; to choose a mode use the segmented control. Do not use a status dot for a decision on a call: that is a badge.

Tags and key-value lists gw-tag gw-tag-list gw-kv

Tags hold values as tokens: allowlist entries (hosts, IPs, CIDRs, schemas), scopes, and the active filters of the log explorer. Literal values use the mono variant. When a tag can be removed, the remove control is a real 24 × 24 button named "Remove <value>". Do not use a tag for a status (badge) or for a choice the user toggles (checkbox, segmented control). Key-value lists show the facts of one object on a native <dl>: connection details, the request block of an event, the summary strip of a call. Do not use them for many objects with the same fields: that is a table.

Invalid and locked entries

An invalid entry takes the danger tone and a leading icon, and the field error names the value. A locked entry keeps its remove button focusable with aria-disabled="true", so the reason can be read out with it.

  • 127.0.0.1
  • localhost
  • 10.20.0.300

10.20.0.300 is not a valid IP address. Fix it or remove it.

127.0.0.1 is the core's own address and cannot be removed.

Markup
<ul class="gw-tag-list" aria-label="Allowed hosts for the local API" aria-describedby="sc-b-tag-invalid">
  <li class="gw-tag gw-tag--mono"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="lock"></i><span class="gw-tag__label">127.0.0.1</span><button class="gw-tag__remove" type="button" aria-label="Remove 127.0.0.1" aria-disabled="true" aria-describedby="sc-b-tag-locked"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="x"></i></button></li>
  <li class="gw-tag gw-tag--mono"><span class="gw-tag__label">localhost</span><button class="gw-tag__remove" type="button" aria-label="Remove localhost"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="x"></i></button></li>
  <li class="gw-tag gw-tag--mono gw-tag--danger"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="circle-alert"></i><span class="gw-tag__label">10.20.0.300</span><button class="gw-tag__remove" type="button" aria-label="Remove 10.20.0.300"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="x"></i></button></li>
</ul>
<p class="gw-text-caption gw-fg-danger" id="sc-b-tag-invalid">10.20.0.300 is not a valid IP address. Fix it or remove it.</p>
<p class="gw-text-caption gw-fg-muted" id="sc-b-tag-locked">127.0.0.1 is the core's own address and cannot be removed.</p>

Stats gw-stat

A KPI tile answers one question at a glance on Overview and Insights: a label, the value with its unit, how it changed and, if useful, a target or a sparkline. The change always carries an icon and words with a sign or direction ("+12% vs yesterday"); its colour comes from what the change means (data-sentiment), not from its direction. A row of tiles is one <dl>. Do not use a stat for a value without context or comparison: a key-value list says it more quietly.

Overview, last 24 hours

1,284

1,201 allowed · 46 approved
Waiting for approval
3
No change vs an hour ago
Oldest auto-denies in 4:12 · Review approvals
Denied by policy
17
+5 vs yesterday
View in Activity
Gateway overhead p95
31 ms
−4 ms vs yesterday
Target ≤ 50 ms · within target

    <dd class="gw-stat__chart">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 96 32" preserveAspectRatio="none" role="img" aria-label="Calls per hour over 24 hours, rising through the afternoon">
        <polyline fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linejoin="round" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke" points="0,26 8,25 16,27 24,22 32,23 40,19 48,20 56,15 64,16 72,11 80,13 88,8 96,9"></polyline>
      </svg>
    </dd>
    <dd class="gw-stat__delta gw-stat__delta--up" data-sentiment="neutral"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="trending-up"></i>+12% vs yesterday</dd>
    <dd class="gw-stat__meta">1,201 allowed · 46 approved</dd>
  </div>
  <div class="gw-stat">

Progress and meters gw-progress gw-meter

Progress shows how far a task has got: setup steps, a plugin upload, the core starting. The page sets the fraction on the root (style="--gw-progress: 0.42") and the ARIA values; with no estimate it is indeterminate. For a short wait in place (a button, Test connection) use a spinner instead. Meter shows an amount against a limit: calls per hour, response size, rows returned. The page compares it with its thresholds and sets data-level; the value is always written out. Neither one is a chart: compare values over time with a chart.

Determinate

Getting started · 5 of 6 steps done

Uploading orders-sync-plugin-1.2.0.jar · 42%

Meter levels

Ok, warn and critical come from the page's thresholds. At warn and critical the value leads with an icon and turns medium weight, so the level never rests on colour; the same words go in aria-valuetext. Without data-level the meter is a plain brand measurement.

Response size · last call 120 KB / 1 MB
Rate limit · endpoint dev 812 / 1,000 calls per hour
Rows returned · sql_query 9,800 / 10,000 rows
Token lifetime used · inspector-debug 27 / 30 days

<div class="gw-meter" role="meter" aria-labelledby="sc-b-meter-size" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="1024" aria-valuenow="120" aria-valuetext="120 KB of 1 MB" data-level="ok" style="--gw-meter: 0.12">
  <span class="gw-meter__label" id="sc-b-meter-size">Response size · last call</span>

  <span class="gw-meter__track"><span class="gw-meter__fill"></span></span>
</div>
<div class="gw-meter" role="meter" aria-labelledby="sc-b-meter-rate" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="1000" aria-valuenow="812" aria-valuetext="812 of 1,000 calls per hour, near the limit" data-level="warn" style="--gw-meter: 0.812">

  <span class="gw-meter__value"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="triangle-alert"></i>812 / 1,000 calls per hour</span>
  <span class="gw-meter__track"><span class="gw-meter__fill"></span></span>
</div>
<div class="gw-meter" role="meter" aria-labelledby="sc-b-meter-rows" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="10000" aria-valuenow="9800" aria-valuetext="9,800 of 10,000 rows, at the limit" data-level="critical" style="--gw-meter: 0.98">

Empty states gw-empty

What will appear here and the one action that fills it. Three situations: a first run (nothing configured yet), a query with no results (filters too narrow) and all clear (nothing waiting). The title states the situation, the text explains what appears here and why it matters, and there is one action at most. Do not use an empty state for a failure: say what happened and what to do in a danger alert.

First run

No connections yet

Connect a database, server, log store or cluster. Agents reach it through an endpoint and never see its secrets.

Fields and inputs gw-field gw-input gw-textarea gw-select gw-input-group

Every value a person types sits in a gw-field: a visible label above the control, a hint under it, and after a failed save an error with an icon, tied to the control with aria-describedby. Controls are native and 32px tall; literal values (hosts, ports, paths) use gw-input--mono. Mark the few optional fields "Optional" instead of starring every required one. Not for values people only read and copy (gw-copy-field) or for secrets (gw-secret); for two to four options that change behaviour use gw-segmented.

Text field states

Hostname or IP the core can reach.

Enter a database name. The core opens it for every call.

Agents see it in the tool list.

Ships with the PostgreSQL connector.

Read only. Audit events refer to it.

Markup
<div class="gw-form__row">
  <div class="gw-field">
    <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-f-host">Host</label>
    <input class="gw-input gw-input--mono" id="sc-c-f-host" value="db.dev.internal" aria-describedby="sc-c-f-host-hint" required autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false">
    <p class="gw-field__hint" id="sc-c-f-host-hint">Hostname or IP the core can reach.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="gw-field">
    <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-f-port">Port</label>
    <input class="gw-input gw-input--mono" id="sc-c-f-port" value="5432" inputmode="numeric" required autocomplete="off">
  </div>
  <div class="gw-field">
    <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-f-db">Database</label>
    <input class="gw-input gw-input--mono" id="sc-c-f-db" value="" placeholder="app" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="sc-c-f-db-err" required autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false">
    <p class="gw-field__error" id="sc-c-f-db-err"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="circle-alert"></i>Enter a database name. The core opens it for every call.</p>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="gw-form__row">
  <div class="gw-field">
    <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-f-desc">Description <span class="gw-field__optional">Optional</span></label>
    <input class="gw-input" id="sc-c-f-desc" placeholder="Orders and billing tables for local work" aria-describedby="sc-c-f-desc-hint">
    <p class="gw-field__hint" id="sc-c-f-desc-hint">Agents see it in the tool list.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="gw-field">

  </div>
  <div class="gw-field">

Textarea, code and counter

Parameters such as :status become typed tool arguments.

Sent to the AI app as the server instructions of endpoint dev. Prose: gw-textarea--wrap, never a sideways scroll.

126 / 2,000

Shorten the note to 140 characters so it fits the Slack and Telegram previews.

147 / 140 · 7 over

Markup
    <div class="gw-field">
      <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-f-sql">SQL template</label>
      <textarea class="gw-textarea gw-textarea--code" id="sc-c-f-sql" rows="5" spellcheck="false" autocapitalize="off" aria-describedby="sc-c-f-sql-hint">
SELECT id, status, created_at
FROM orders
WHERE created_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
  AND status = :status
LIMIT :limit</textarea>
      <p class="gw-field__hint" id="sc-c-f-sql-hint">Parameters such as <code class="gw-code">:status</code> become typed tool arguments.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="gw-field">
      <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-f-instr">Instructions for agents <span class="gw-field__optional">Optional</span></label>
      <textarea class="gw-textarea gw-textarea--wrap" id="sc-c-f-instr" rows="3" maxlength="2000" aria-describedby="sc-c-f-instr-hint sc-c-f-instr-count">Use dev-db for order data. Prefer sql_query for reads. Before any UPDATE, say which rows it touches and wait for the approval.</textarea>
      <p class="gw-field__hint" id="sc-c-f-instr-hint">Sent to the AI app as the server instructions of endpoint <code class="gw-code">dev</code>. Prose: <code class="gw-code">gw-textarea--wrap</code>, never a sideways scroll.</p>
      <p class="gw-field__counter" id="sc-c-f-instr-count">126 / 2,000</p>
    </div>

Checkbox, radio, switch gw-checkbox gw-radio gw-switch

The native input does the work and is stretched, transparent, over the whole choice, so the box, the label and the hint are one target at least 24px tall. Checkbox: a value saved with the form, several independent options, "select all" (indeterminate is a property, set from script: [indeterminate] in Angular). Radio: one of a few options that each need a sentence; with an icon and a description use gw-choice-card, with one word each use gw-segmented. Switch: a setting that applies at once, with no Save; never inside a form that has a Save button. Dependent options under a "select all" sit in gw-field--nested; in a table the selection column uses the box without a label (gw-table). Unavailable, with a reason: aria-disabled="true" + aria-describedby on the input (the hint says why); it looks like disabled, stays in the Tab order, and kit.js keeps it from toggling. Native disabled only when there is nothing to explain.

Segmented control gw-segmented

A real radio group drawn as joined segments: Tab lands on the checked option, arrow keys move and select, the value submits with the form, no script. The main case is the tool mode Off · Read only · Approval · Bypass; Bypass runs calls without approval, including changes to data. The checked option takes its tone from data-tone (off neutral, read info, approval warning, or any tone name such as dev, stage, prod) with an edge in the tone colour, semibold text and its own icon, so the choice never rests on a tint alone. Without data-tone it is brand, for plain view switches. For a mutating tool Read only is disabled and the reason is visible next to the control and linked with aria-describedby. Not for switching views of a panel (that is gw-tabs--contained) or for more than four options (use gw-select).

Tool mode

sql_query readOnly
Mode for sql_query
sql_execute destructive
Mode for sql_execute

Read only is unavailable: sql_execute changes data, so choose Approval, Bypass or Off.

sql_query prod

Locked by the prod policy of endpoint incident-prod: prod-replica is read only.

    </label>
                  <label class="gw-segmented__option" data-tone="bypass"><input class="gw-segmented__input" type="radio" name="sc-c-mode-default" value="bypass" title="Run without approval; policy limits still apply"><span class="gw-segmented__label"><i class="gw-icon gw-icon--sm" data-lucide="shield-off"></i>Bypass</span></label>
  </div>
  <p class="gw-field__hint">Tools a connector adds later start in this mode. Off is the safest default.</p>
</fieldset>

Secret gw-secret

Credentials are write-only: once saved, the value is never shown again, here or in the API, and the agent never sees it. data-state picks what the field shows; the frame stays 32px tall so switching state does not move the form. A reveal toggle exists only while a brand new value is typed (aria-pressed on an input-group addon). A stored secret offers Replace and Rotate, never "show". Not for one-time tokens the user must copy (gw-copy-field--secret-once) or for masked values in results (gw-code--secret).

Stored

Password
Encrypted version 3 · updated 2 days ago

Decrypted inside the connector only for the duration of a call.

Choice cards gw-choice-card

A radio or checkbox drawn as a card, for choices that need an icon and a sentence: connection type, secret source, environment. The native input covers the card, so a click anywhere selects it and arrow keys move between radio cards. Checked = 2px brand border, brand tint and a filled indicator with a check; keyboard focus rings the whole card. Name the input with aria-labelledby (title) and aria-describedby (description) when the card has more than a title. Lay cards out with gw-grid inside fieldset.gw-field. For one-word options use gw-segmented; for options that need no explanation use gw-radio.

Search and file drop gw-search gw-file-drop

Search filters a list or table as you type and is the input of the command palette: icon at the start, a clear button once it has a value, an optional key hint while empty. The placeholder is required (clear and hint key off :placeholder-shown) and the input is named with aria-label; for structured queries (decision:denied tool:sql_*) the same field sits in log-explorer. File drop uploads a plugin JAR, an OpenAPI document or a kubeconfig: a label around a transparent input type="file", so click, keyboard and a dropped file all work without script; the app sets data-state. Actions on an uploaded file (remove, replace) go outside the label: a label must not contain buttons.

Search: empty, with a value, disabled

/

    <button class="gw-search__clear" type="button" aria-label="Clear search"><i class="gw-icon gw-icon--sm" data-lucide="x"></i></button>

Form layout gw-form

Sections of fields, each with a title and one paragraph that says what it controls. Below 1280px everything stacks; from lg the title and description take the left third and the fields the right two thirds. A section is a fieldset whose legend names it; fields that belong together sit side by side in gw-form__row. Forms that save on a button use --sticky-actions: while there are unsaved changes, "Unsaved changes" with Discard and Save floats at the bottom of the scrolling area. Settings that apply at once use gw-switch and need no Save. (The demo form uses method="dialog" so Save does not reload the showcase.)

Markup
<form class="gw-form gw-form--sticky-actions" method="dialog" aria-label="Edit connection dev-db">
  <fieldset class="gw-form__section">
    <legend class="gw-form__legend">Connection</legend>
    <p class="gw-form__description">Where the core reaches the database. It connects from this machine, so your VPN and hosts file apply.</p>
    <div class="gw-form__rows">
      <div class="gw-form__row">
        <div class="gw-field">
          <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-fm-host">Host</label>
          <input class="gw-input gw-input--mono" id="sc-c-fm-host" value="db.dev.internal" required autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false">
        </div>
        <div class="gw-field">
          <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-fm-port">Port</label>
          <input class="gw-input gw-input--mono" id="sc-c-fm-port" value="5432" inputmode="numeric" required autocomplete="off">
        </div>
        <div class="gw-field">
          <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-fm-db">Database</label>
          <input class="gw-input gw-input--mono" id="sc-c-fm-db" value="app" required autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="gw-field">
        <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-fm-ssl">SSL mode</label>
        <select class="gw-select" id="sc-c-fm-ssl">
          <option value="require">Require</option>
          <option value="verify-full" selected>Verify CA and host name</option>
        </select>
      </div>
    </div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="gw-form__section">
    <legend class="gw-form__legend">Credentials</legend>
    <p class="gw-form__description">The agent never sees these. Use a database user that can only read wherever you can.</p>
    <div class="gw-form__rows">
      <div class="gw-field">
        <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-fm-user">User</label>
        <input class="gw-input gw-input--mono" id="sc-c-fm-user" value="gw_reader" required autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false">
      </div>
      <div class="gw-field">
        <span class="gw-field__label" id="sc-c-fm-pw-l">Password</span>
        <div class="gw-secret" data-state="stored" role="group" aria-labelledby="sc-c-fm-pw-l">
          <span class="gw-secret__status"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="lock-keyhole"></i>Encrypted</span>
          <span class="gw-secret__meta">version <span class="gw-mono">3</span> · updated <time datetime="2026-10-20T09:14:00Z" title="2026-10-20 09:14 UTC">2 days ago</time></span>
          <span class="gw-secret__actions">
            <button class="gw-btn gw-btn--ghost gw-btn--sm" type="button" aria-label="Replace password for dev-db">Replace</button>
            <button class="gw-btn gw-btn--ghost gw-btn--sm" type="button" aria-label="Rotate password for dev-db">Rotate</button>
          </span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="gw-form__section">
    <legend class="gw-form__legend">Environment and safety</legend>
    <p class="gw-form__description">Prod turns on strict defaults: a read-only user check, row limit 100 and an approval for every mutation.</p>
    <div class="gw-form__rows">
      <fieldset class="gw-field">
        <legend class="gw-field__label">Environment</legend>
        <div class="gw-form__row">
          <label class="gw-choice-card gw-choice-card--compact">
            <input class="gw-choice-card__input" type="radio" name="sc-c-fm-env" value="dev" checked>
            <span class="gw-choice-card__title"><span class="gw-env gw-env--dev">dev</span> Development</span>
          </label>
          <label class="gw-choice-card gw-choice-card--compact">
            <input class="gw-choice-card__input" type="radio" name="sc-c-fm-env" value="stage">
            <span class="gw-choice-card__title"><span class="gw-env gw-env--stage">stage</span> Staging</span>
          </label>
          <label class="gw-choice-card gw-choice-card--compact">
            <input class="gw-choice-card__input" type="radio" name="sc-c-fm-env" value="prod">
            <span class="gw-choice-card__title"><span class="gw-env gw-env--prod">prod</span> Production</span>
          </label>
        </div>
      </fieldset>
      <div class="gw-field">
        <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-c-fm-timeout">Statement timeout</label>
        <div class="gw-input-group">
          <input class="gw-input gw-input--mono" id="sc-c-fm-timeout" value="5000" inputmode="numeric" aria-describedby="sc-c-fm-timeout-hint">
          <span class="gw-input-group__affix">ms</span>
        </div>
        <p class="gw-field__hint" id="sc-c-fm-timeout-hint">The database cancels slower statements.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="gw-checkbox">
        <input class="gw-checkbox__input" type="checkbox" id="sc-c-fm-mask" checked aria-describedby="sc-c-fm-mask-hint">
        <span class="gw-checkbox__control" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        <label class="gw-checkbox__label" for="sc-c-fm-mask">Mask personal data in results</label>
        <p class="gw-checkbox__hint" id="sc-c-fm-mask-hint">Emails and phone numbers become ‹masked› before the agent sees them.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </fieldset>

  <div class="gw-form__actions">
    <p class="gw-form__note" role="status"><i class="gw-icon" data-lucide="circle-dot"></i>Unsaved changes</p>
    <button class="gw-btn" type="reset">Discard</button>
    <button class="gw-btn gw-btn--primary" type="submit">Save connection</button>
  </div>
</form>

Tabs gw-tabs

Sibling views of one object on one page: the endpoint's Tools & policies, Tokens, AI apps and Settings. The selected tab has three cues, not one: a 2px brand bar, primary text and semibold weight. Arrow keys move and select, Home and End jump, the panel follows. Contained tabs switch the view of the same data (Activity: Events or Traces) and fit a 32px toolbar row. Do not use tabs for the steps of a flow (gw-stepper), to move between pages (gw-nav) or for a setting with two or three values (gw-segmented).

Menus and popovers gw-menu-host gw-menu gw-popover

The kit's only dropdown. A menu holds actions on one object; a listbox picks one value and shows a check; a popover holds a small form next to its trigger (add a filter). All three open on click, Enter or Space, never on hover or focus. Arrows move, Home and End jump, Esc closes and returns focus to the trigger, Tab or a click outside closes. A danger item never acts by itself: it opens a confirmation. Do not use a menu to move between pages, to hide the one main action of a view, or to choose between two or three always-visible options (gw-segmented).

Tooltip gw-tooltip

A short, non-essential hint next to its trigger: the name of an icon-only button, the absolute time behind "3 min ago", why a control is unavailable. CSS only: it shows on hover (after a beat) and at once on keyboard focus, and the pointer can move onto it. When the tooltip is the name, point aria-labelledby at it; when it adds information, use aria-describedby. Never put links, buttons or anything needed to finish a task in a tooltip (it is not interactive and not reachable by touch): use a popover or inline text instead.

Explain an unavailable control

stage-db reads its password from vault://kv/stage/db#password. Rotate it in Vault.

aria-disabled, not disabled: the button stays focusable, so keyboard users get the reason too. When the reason matters to the task (a tool mode that is unavailable), write it next to the control instead.

Markup

</span>
<p class="gw-text-caption gw-fg-muted"><code class="gw-code">aria-disabled</code>, not <code class="gw-code">disabled</code>: the button stays focusable, so keyboard users get the reason too. When the reason matters to the task (a tool mode that is unavailable), write it next to the control instead.</p>

Dialogs and drawers gw-dialog gw-drawer

Native <dialog> opened with showModal(): focus moves in and stays, Esc closes, the page behind is inert, and focus returns to the opener. A dialog asks one question or holds one short task: confirm a revoke, create an endpoint. A drawer slides in from the right to read beside the list: the detail of an event, a trace. Do not use a dialog for content people compare with the page (use a drawer or gw-split), for long multi-step setup (a page with gw-stepper) or to report success (gw-toast). Every dialog names its initial focus in the markup: autofocus on the first field of a form, or on Cancel in a confirmation (danger and warning alike), so Enter never confirms by accident.

Confirm a risky but reversible action

gw-dialog--warning: publish the tunnel, change the port, accept calls from any address. The confirm is a normal primary button, never danger, and the dialog lists exactly what changes. Installing an unsigned plugin or reviewing an external MCP server is not this: unverified code runs on this computer as your user, so those use gw-dialog--danger.

Publish stage-readonly to the internet?

A tunnel gives it a public HTTPS address. Three gates stay in front: Anthropic IP ranges only, each sign-in allowed on this computer, and the endpoint's own read-only modes.

Sizes

Create endpoint

One URL for a set of connections, tools and modes. Add tools and tokens next.

URL: http://127.0.0.1:7465/mcp/stage-readonly

PostgreSQL connector · 4 tools

Built-in · v1.4.0 · signed. Tools that change data wait for approval by default; the body scrolls, the header and footer stay.

sql_list_schemas
List schemas and tables the connection user can see.
sql_describe_table
Columns, types, indexes and foreign keys of one table.
sql_query
Run one read-only SELECT within the policy's row limit and statement timeout (dev 1,000 rows, prod 100 rows and 3 s); PII columns are masked.
sql_execute
INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE. Always needs approval; DDL is denied on prod.

Toasts and alerts gw-toast gw-alert

A toast reports the result of something the user just did, or an event that needs no answer now, and leaves after 6 s. It is never the only place a decision or an error lives: approvals stay in Approvals, a failing connection keeps its alert. Reversible actions show a toast with Undo instead of a confirmation. An alert describes a state that holds while it is true: inline in a section or form, or as a banner above the page for app-wide state (Core stopped, Tunnel is public). Both say what happened and what to do; the tone is never the only cue, the icon and the words say it too.

Live toasts

Stepper gw-stepper

Where the user is in a short linear flow of three to five steps: Add connection, first-run onboarding. With --guide it is a two- or three-step first-run guide whose steps carry their own actions. An ordered list; the current step carries aria-current="step", and completed or failed steps say so in sr-only text, not only with the check or the cross. Horizontal from 960px, vertical below it or always with --vertical. It shows progress, it is not navigation: going back is a Back button. Do not use it for views of equal weight (gw-tabs) or for an open-ended checklist (getting-started).

Add connection

  1. Choose type, completed PostgreSQL
  2. 2 Configure dev-db · dev
  3. 3 Test
  4. 4 Add to endpoint

Pagination gw-paginator

Three patterns on one block. Compact: the range and previous / next, under tables that sort and filter on the server. Numbered: pages for short lists people browse, like the connector catalog. Load older: the audit log uses a cursor, never page numbers, because new events arrive at the top and loading older rows below never moves what you are reading. Name the nav after its list and announce the new range after a change. Do not paginate fewer than about 50 rows: show them all.

Skeleton gw-skeleton

Placeholder in the shape of content that is about to arrive, for the first render of a list, a card or a chart when the wait passes about 300 ms. A calm opacity pulse, never a shimmer sweep, at half speed with reduced motion. The blocks are aria-hidden; the region carries aria-busy="true" and an sr-only status names what is loading. Use a spinner for in-place actions (Test connection), gw-progress for long jobs, and never a skeleton for content that failed: show the error with gw-alert--danger.

--circle

Code gw-code gw-code-block gw-tok-*

Literal values are shown verbatim in JetBrains Mono with ligatures off: what a human approves or copies is exactly what runs. Use gw-code for one literal inside a sentence, a table cell or a heading (tool names, slugs, hosts, paths, token prefixes). Use gw-code-block for anything multi-line: the exact statement in an approval request, a config snippet, command output. Do not use either for emphasis, for keyboard shortcuts (gw-kbd) or for a value the user edits (gw-textarea--code). Masked values are never real secrets: they render as ‹masked›.

Inline literal

Codex called sql_query on dev-db (db.dev.internal:5432/app) as codex-laptop (a 15-minute token issued on the fly). The password stays in the gateway: ‹masked›.

Markup
<p class="gw-text-body-read">Codex called <code class="gw-code">sql_query</code> on <code class="gw-code">dev-db</code> (<code class="gw-code">db.dev.internal:5432/app</code>) as <code class="gw-code">codex-laptop</code> (a 15-minute token issued on the fly). The password stays in the gateway: <code class="gw-code gw-code--secret">‹masked›</code>.</p>

SQL with copy

The copy button reads the <pre> through data-gw-copy-from; for 1.6 s it carries [data-copied] and shows its "Copied" face. The body is a keyboard-scrollable region.

SQL sql_query · dev-db 
-- requested by Codex · trace 4f2a9c
SELECT id, status
FROM orders
WHERE created_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
LIMIT 50

Syntax tokens

Token colours come from --gw-color-code-*, each at least 4.5:1 on the code background in all four modes. Colour is decoration here: the text itself is the content. A block can omit the header.

gw-tok-keyword      SELECT, WHERE, true, null
gw-tok-string       'cancelled', "POST"
gw-tok-number       48213, 1.5
gw-tok-comment      -- comments, # comments
gw-tok-function     now(), count(*)
gw-tok-property     JSON, YAML and TOML keys
gw-tok-punctuation  , ; ( ) = { } [ ]
gw-tok-secret       ‹masked›, ‹masked:pii›, ‹secret:vault://kv/stage/db#password›
Markup

      <div class="gw-code-block__body" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Syntax token reference">
<pre class="gw-code-block__pre"><code><span class="gw-tok-keyword">gw-tok-keyword</span>      SELECT, WHERE, true, null
<span class="gw-tok-string">gw-tok-string</span>       'cancelled', "POST"
<span class="gw-tok-number">gw-tok-number</span>       48213, 1.5
<span class="gw-tok-comment">gw-tok-comment</span>      -- comments, # comments
<span class="gw-tok-function">gw-tok-function</span>     now(), count(*)
<span class="gw-tok-property">gw-tok-property</span>     JSON, YAML and TOML keys
<span class="gw-tok-punctuation">gw-tok-punctuation</span>  , ; ( ) = { } [ ]
<span class="gw-tok-secret">gw-tok-secret</span>       ‹masked›, ‹masked:pii›, ‹secret:vault://kv/stage/db#password›</code></pre>
      </div>
    </div>

Hidden and look-alike characters

Text a human confirms must be visible, not only verbatim. A bidi override, a zero-width character, a tab or a trailing space renders as a boxed escape (gw-tok-invisible); a non-ASCII letter that looks like ASCII is boxed as itself (gw-tok-confusable). Both carry the code point in title, and a warning above the block counts them.

UPDATE оrders SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id = 48213;‹U+202E›
‹TAB›SELECT 1;‹U+200B›‹SP›
Markup
    <div class="gw-code-block gw-code-block--wrap">
      <div class="gw-code-block__body" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Statement with hidden characters shown">
<pre class="gw-code-block__pre"><code><span class="gw-code-block__line"><span class="gw-tok-keyword">UPDATE</span> <span class="gw-tok-confusable" title="U+043E Cyrillic small letter o">о</span>rders <span class="gw-tok-keyword">SET</span> status <span class="gw-tok-punctuation">=</span> <span class="gw-tok-string">'cancelled'</span> <span class="gw-tok-keyword">WHERE</span> id <span class="gw-tok-punctuation">=</span> <span class="gw-tok-number">48213</span><span class="gw-tok-punctuation">;</span><span class="gw-tok-invisible" title="U+202E right-to-left override">‹U+202E›</span></span>
<span class="gw-code-block__line"><span class="gw-tok-invisible" title="U+0009 character tabulation">‹TAB›</span><span class="gw-tok-keyword">SELECT</span> <span class="gw-tok-number">1</span><span class="gw-tok-punctuation">;</span><span class="gw-tok-invisible" title="U+200B zero width space">‹U+200B›</span><span class="gw-tok-invisible" title="U+0020 trailing space">‹SP›</span></span></code></pre>
      </div>
    </div>

Diff gw-diff

A unified diff of the exact change a human confirms: what "Connect" writes into an AI app's config, what k8s_apply changes in a manifest. Every changed line carries a + or − marker as text and a spoken "Added" / "Removed" prefix, so the change survives greyscale, high contrast and screen readers; the washes are the second cue. Line text keeps the code colour. Use it for changes, not for showing a whole file (that is a gw-code-block).

Copy field gw-copy-field

A read-only value the user takes somewhere else: an endpoint URL, a command for MCP Inspector, a token in the one moment it is visible. The "Copy" button reads the value through data-gw-copy-from, switches to "Copied" for 1.6 s and announces it. Do not use it for values the user edits (an input), for stored secrets (they are write-only: gw-secret) or for long snippets (a gw-code-block).

Endpoint URL

Name the field with a visible label: a role="group" + aria-labelledby around a <code> value, or a <label for> when the value is an <input readonly> (focusable, select all with the keyboard).

Endpoint URL

http://127.0.0.1:7465/mcp/dev
Markup
<p class="gw-text-ui" id="sc-e-cf-url-label">Endpoint URL</p>
<div class="gw-copy-field" role="group" aria-labelledby="sc-e-cf-url-label">
  <code class="gw-copy-field__value" id="sc-e-cf-url">http://127.0.0.1:7465/mcp/dev</code>
  <button class="gw-btn gw-btn--sm gw-copy-field__button" type="button" data-gw-copy-from="#sc-e-cf-url">
    <span class="gw-copy-field__copy"><i class="gw-icon gw-icon--sm" data-lucide="copy"></i> Copy<span class="gw-sr-only"> endpoint URL</span></span>
    <span class="gw-copy-field__copied"><i class="gw-icon gw-icon--sm" data-lucide="check"></i> Copied</span>
  </button>
</div>

Read-only input in a field

  <label class="gw-field__label" for="sc-e-cf-cmd">Connect MCP Inspector</label>
  <div class="gw-copy-field">
    <input class="gw-copy-field__value" id="sc-e-cf-cmd" type="text" readonly value="npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --transport http --server-url http://127.0.0.1:7465/mcp/dev">
    <button class="gw-btn gw-btn--sm gw-copy-field__button" type="button" data-gw-copy-from="#sc-e-cf-cmd">
      <span class="gw-copy-field__copy"><i class="gw-icon gw-icon--sm" data-lucide="copy"></i> Copy<span class="gw-sr-only"> Inspector command</span></span>
      <span class="gw-copy-field__copied"><i class="gw-icon gw-icon--sm" data-lucide="check"></i> Copied</span>
    </button>
  </div>
</div>

Copied state

Shown here with a static data-copied; in the app kit.js sets and clears it.

http://127.0.0.1:7465/mcp/dev

  </button>
</div>

Token, shown once

--secret-once is the result step of issuing a token: the full value is visible and wraps, because this is the only moment it can be copied. After the dialog closes, the token appears only by its prefix gwt_Vb8r…. Claude Desktop and Codex never see this step: they get short-lived tokens on the fly.

Token cursor-laptop

gwt_Vb8rT2kLq9XwN4cZ7mHs1PdF6yJa3eUg5RiK0oBt

Shown once. Store it in your password manager.

Markup
<p class="gw-text-ui" id="sc-e-cf-token-label">Token cursor-laptop</p>
<div class="gw-copy-field gw-copy-field--secret-once" role="group" aria-labelledby="sc-e-cf-token-label">
  <code class="gw-copy-field__value" id="sc-e-cf-token">gwt_Vb8rT2kLq9XwN4cZ7mHs1PdF6yJa3eUg5RiK0oBt</code>
  <button class="gw-btn gw-btn--sm gw-copy-field__button" type="button" data-gw-copy-from="#sc-e-cf-token" aria-describedby="sc-e-cf-token-hint">
    <span class="gw-copy-field__copy"><i class="gw-icon gw-icon--sm" data-lucide="copy"></i> Copy<span class="gw-sr-only"> token</span></span>
    <span class="gw-copy-field__copied"><i class="gw-icon gw-icon--sm" data-lucide="check"></i> Copied</span>
  </button>
  <p class="gw-copy-field__hint" id="sc-e-cf-token-hint"><i class="gw-icon gw-icon--sm" data-lucide="triangle-alert"></i>Shown once. Store it in your password manager.</p>
</div>

Table gw-table-wrap gw-table

A native <table> for dense, sortable lists of objects with the same fields: calls in Activity, connections, tokens, secrets. Screen readers get real rows and columns; sorting is a button inside th[aria-sort]; selection mirrors to tr[aria-selected]. The wrap is the scroller, so it is a named, focusable region. Do not use a table for one object's facts (a gw-kv list) or for a handful of rich items with actions (cards).

Sortable, with row selection

Click a header to sort; the icon follows aria-sort and the order is announced. The checkbox column uses data-gw-select-all and data-gw-select-row; a selected row gets the selected fill and a brand bar. Decisions are badges with icon and words; environments sit right after the connection name.

Interactive rows

--interactive: each row opens the event detail. The link sits in the first cell and stretches over the row; the focus ring is drawn on the row. Row actions stay visible (never on hover only) and remain clickable above the link. Here Time is sorted ascending (oldest first), as a trace reads. The row whose drawer is open carries aria-current="true" on its row link and gets the selected fill and brand bar; tr[aria-selected] is only for checkbox selection. Copy link copies gaterook://activity/events/<id>.

Narrow window: optional columns, scroll shadows, a pinned action

If the table is still wider than its wrap, a soft shade marks the edge that has more behind it. In a full-width alert row the action cell is __cell--sticky-end, so “Test again” stays reachable.

Charts gw-chart gw-legend gw-sparkline

Lightweight charts in HTML, CSS and inline SVG, no library: a stacked histogram of calls over time, a horizontal bar list for top tools, a sparkline inside a stat. Data enters as unitless custom properties (style="--v: 0.42", value ÷ axis max). Every chart is role="img" with an aria-label that states the finding, and the numbers sit next to it in a visually hidden table. Series differ by more than colour: legend words, a fixed stack order and 1px gaps. Marks paint with tone FG tokens or --gw-color-chart-1…6, never solids. Use a chart when the shape matters (a spike, a ranking); when one number matters, use a gw-stat; when exact values matter, use a table.

Interactive histogram

In the log explorer a column narrows the time range. Then the bars are buttons with an aria-label each: the labels carry the numbers (they replace the hidden table), so the root is a role="group", not an image. aria-pressed="true" marks the selected range with a fill and a brand bar on top; hover washes the column and focus rings it. Columns may get narrower than 24px, so the time-range picker next to the histogram stays the equivalent control.

100 200

Legend

The swatch takes the same modifiers as a segment: decision tones for status series, --series-1…6 for categories, and --hatch for idle time (the approval wait in a waterfall). A waterfall legend names its phases with the span tones: --neutral Gateway, --brand Resource. The words carry the meaning; an optional gw-legend__value gives the total.

  • Logs 341

Waterfall gw-waterfall

Where the time of one call went: the gateway's own work (authentication, policy, secret, masking), time inside the resource, and the idle wait for a human decision. Rows are phases in order (<ol>); each reads as "phase, duration", and the bar is decoration. Spans are placed with --start and --len as fractions of the total and are never thinner than 2px. Use it in event details; for latency across many calls use a chart.

Read call, allowed

  1. Authenticate token and check policy 2 ms
  2. Decrypt secret for dev-db 1 ms
  3. Query on dev-db 31 ms
  4. Mask result and respond 4 ms
  • Gateway
  • Resource

Timeline gw-timeline

A vertical feed of what happened, in order: the path of an approval request from request to execution, the steps of an agent trace. It is an <ol>; each item has a toned marker with an icon from the decision vocabulary, a title that says what happened in words, meta, and a <time datetime>. The step a request is in right now carries aria-current="step": filled marker and a heavier title. Use it for history; for the steps of a form or wizard use gw-stepper.
